content:
Claude Code's auto mode will become the default permission setting for users next week.

Starting August 14, sessions for Pro, Max, and Team users will use auto mode, unless users or admins have locked in other settings.

Anthropic will no longer charge for the additional tokens generated by the auto mode classifier with each tool call.

According to Anthropic, auto mode uses a classifier to replace recurring approval prompts, checking whether each tool call involves irreversible, destructive, or out-of-bounds actions.

If the classifier intercepts an action, Claude can attempt a safer approach or request permission from the user. After multiple interceptions, the session falls back to manual approval mode.

As part of this change, Anthropic says it will no longer charge for the "small number of additional tokens per tool call" generated by the auto mode classifier.

Anthropic says it studied 1,053 paid testers and found that humans only intercepted 13.6% of dangerous instructions, while auto mode intercepted 89%. After 50 prompts, human performance dropped to about 5%.

However, Anthropic also notes that the classifier cannot completely eliminate risk, and recommends that production changes still be manually reviewed.

This adjustment is expected to make long task execution with Claude Code more practical, and will combine with its regular workflows, voice mode, and the browser built into the Mac app. Anthropic says Team and Enterprise customers using auto mode submit about 25% more pull requests.

9to5Mac's take

Although it sounds risky, this may be a reasonable default for experienced users. However, users should build a certain level of trust with the coding agent before relying on auto mode.

It's also worth noting that Anthropic has taken this step. For comparison, OpenAI at one point chose to turn off auto mode for their most powerful GPT-5.6 version as an extra precaution.
